content.introduction: In May 2026, the S&P 500 rose 10.5%, driven by strong economic growth and leadership changes at the Federal Reserve, despite rising oil prices and geopolitical tensions. Emerging markets led with a 9.7% increase. Sector performance was mixed, with many sectors declining.
body: Rising oil prices increased inflationary pressures, reducing expectations for near-term rate cuts despite solid economic growth and leadership changes at the Federal Reserve. Stock investors who either held steady through April’s fluctuations or wrote off the early weeks of our conflict with Iran as a passing or inconsequential phenomenon were rewarded as the S&P 500 rose 10.5%, reversing the losses of March as the year-to-date return bounced back to 5.7%. While oil prices and daily stock valuations fluctuated with the fortunes of war and the oscillating news regarding the Strait of Hormuz, the underlying strength of the U.S. economy, corporate earnings, and labor market supported the steady upward trend for the stock market. Large oil companies stand to join the earnings winners as they benefit from higher crude and gas prices, which could remain elevated for some time, even if the conflict in the Middle East is settled. As higher oil prices percolate through the economy, expectations for future rate cuts have continued to drop, in spite of the shift in leadership at the Federal Reserve.
